% Shared LaTeX scaffolding for paper figures. DO NOT edit per-figure.
% Compiles a single tikzpicture (passed via \figfile) into a tightly
% cropped, paper-ready PDF. Drive it through build_pdf.sh, which sets
% \figfile and TEXINPUTS for you.
%
%   pdflatex "\def\figfile{myfigure.tex}\input{main.tex}"
%
\documentclass[tikz,border=2pt]{standalone}

% --- Font: Carlito (metric-compatible Calibri clone) as the default ---
\usepackage{carlito}
\renewcommand{\familydefault}{\sfdefault}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}

% --- Math that matches the sans text ---
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage{sansmath}
\sansmath

% --- TikZ / pgfplots with the libraries figures commonly need ---
\usepackage{tikz}
\usepackage{pgfplots}
\pgfplotsset{compat=1.18}
\usetikzlibrary{calc,positioning,arrows.meta,patterns,fit,backgrounds}
\usepgfplotslibrary{groupplots,fillbetween}

% A consistent, color-blind-safe palette available to every figure as
% c0..c5 (Okabe-Ito). Use these instead of raw red/green/blue.
\definecolor{c0}{HTML}{0072B2} % blue
\definecolor{c1}{HTML}{E69F00} % orange
\definecolor{c2}{HTML}{009E73} % green
\definecolor{c3}{HTML}{D55E00} % vermillion
\definecolor{c4}{HTML}{CC79A7} % purple
\definecolor{c5}{HTML}{56B4E9} % sky blue

\begin{document}
\input{\figfile}
\end{document}
